Maria G. (Finance): quick question — we're down to NomadSpend and BillPrism for the invoice/usage reconciliation tool RFP. Execs want a simple TCO scorecard by EOD Friday. Can someone take lead on the cost matrix?
Kevin L. (Procurement): I can own the price inputs. Need list of what to include (one-time migration, seat vs usage, overage mechanics, export costs, support SLAs).
Ahmad R. (EngOps): for EngOps: add GPU/compute credits? jk. Seriously tho: need integration effort (SFTP, API, webhook), sample payload sizes, and time to spin up pipelines.
Sofia T. (Product): add feature weightings: invoice parsing accuracy, allowances for custom SKUs, business-unit tagging, multi-currency handling. Also audit log fidelity (for compliance).
Maria G. (Finance): perfect. I'll draft a scoring template. Initial weights: Cost 40%, Integration effort 20%, Features 25%, Compliance/SLAs 15%. open to tweaks. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Kevin L. (Procurement): fine by me. For pricing rows I need these columns: Vendor list price, Negotiated baseline (we estimate), Commit discount tiers, Overages per unit, Data egress fees, Export/lookup API cost, Annual maintenance fee.
Ahmad R. (EngOps): and these technical rows: Auth methods (SSO/SAML/OIDC), Webhook concurrency limits, Bulk export (>10GB) handling, Sample latency for 1k invoice batch, CSV/JSON schema stability.
Sofia T. (Product): add evaluation row: "manual review rate" (how often parser needs human correction) and "training/update cadence" — are they retraining models per customer?
Maria G. (Finance): ok I'll put those into a short matrix. Draft snippet below — feel free to copy/paste and edit: ```
Metric | Weight | NomadSpend (score) | BillPrism (score)
Cost (5yr TCO) | 40% | 65 | 78
Integration effort | 20% | 70 | 50
Features (parsing, tagging) | 25% | 80 | 68
Compliance & SLAs | 15% | 90 | 60
Notes: scores 0-100, higher better.```
Kevin L. (Procurement): helpful. I'll fill pricing rows by EOD. Quick ask: does either vendor force a minimum commit? NomadSpend mentioned a 12k/mo minimum. BillPrism is purely usage-based but has a 6-month minimum for enterprise onboarding.
Sofia T. (Product): NomadSpend's demo showed better custody of line-item mapping (fewer manual touches). BillPrism had a nicer UI for auditors and better export formats.
Ahmad R. (EngOps): FYI, BillPrism needs a connector build for our data lake (no native connector), NomadSpend already has a Snowflake-to-API publisher. Implementation delta ≈ 2 engineer-weeks for BillPrism.
Maria G. (Finance): noted. Kevin — for negotiation leverage, do we have any reference customers or case studies to push on pricing?
Kevin L. (Procurement): vendor-bot pulled some notes: vendor-bot: "NomadSpend: 50+ mid-market customers, two SOC2 reports; BillPrism: 30 customers, SOC2 in progress, offers 10% discount for commitment"
Maria G. (Finance): good — let's assume 10% baseline negotiable for both. Also include amortized migration cost (estimate $18k one-time for mapping + QA).
Sofia T. (Product): ROI note: with current invoice volume, break-even on NomadSpend commit happens in ~10 months due to lower processing unit cost. I'll add that to the comments column.
Ahmad R. (EngOps): can we get sample invoices from both vendors for accuracy benchmark? NomadSpend shared 500-sample set in demo. BillPrism asked for an NDA before samples.
Kevin L. (Procurement): I'll handle NDA request with BillPrism today. If we can't get samples, reduce their parsing score conservatively.
Maria G. (Finance): timeline: Kevin fills pricing rows; Ahmad fills integration effort; Sofia fills product/accuracy notes. I'll assemble final scorecard and share with execs Friday 3pm.
Sofia T. (Product): ack. small ask — include fallback options (manual processing fallback cost) and SLA credits if parser breaks — ops wants clear remediation.
Maria G. (Finance): added. Any other blockers?
Ahmad R. (EngOps): one more: export retention — BillPrism had 30-day raw export retention on lower tier, NomadSpend 90 days. That will affect storage/archival cost in TCO.
Maria G. (Finance): good catch — I'll add retention cost assumptions.
Kevin L. (Procurement): on it. Will ping if vendors push hard on minimums. :thumbsup:
Maria G. (Finance): thanks team — will post draft scorecard here when ready and @channel the exec snapshot.
